# A grouped block whose `amount:` is not the sum of the splits it names.
#
# README: "`amount:` on such a block is the sum of the splits it names", and
# the reason is that the same file has to mean one thing in two books. In the
# book that holds the transaction the named splits settle the invoice by their
# own figures — 60 and 40, so 100. In a book that does not, the guids resolve
# to nothing and the payment is entered from the block, so `amount: 60` books
# 60 for money that moved 100.
#
# Nothing weighed it. The in-book path matches a naming block by guid, so
# `_single_payment_matches` — the only thing that reads `amount:` — never runs,
# and the grouped branch checked existence, account, lot, owner and the total
# against what is owed without ever looking at the stated figure. Every sibling
# spelling weighs it, including the parked single-split path; this was the one
# that skipped it.
#
# What this fixture produces: a refusal quoting the 60.00 stated and the 100.00
# the named splits come to.
#
# Verified by
# tests/integration/test_linking_a_split_not_on_the_receivable.py.
invoice "INV-USD-001"
  customer_id: "C-US"
  currency: USD
  date_opened: 2026-01-05
  entry:
    date: 2026-01-05
    description: "Consulting"
    action: "Hours"
    account: "Income:Sales"
    quantity: 1
    price: 100
    taxable: false
    tax_included: false
  posted:
    date: 2026-01-05
    due: 2026-02-05
    ar_account: "Assets:Accounts Receivable USD"
    memo: "Invoice INV-USD-001"
    accumulate: true
  payment:
    date: 2026-02-27
    amount: 60
    account: "Assets:Bank:USD"
    Transaction "5e6f708192a3b4c5d6e7f80912233445"
      PaymentSplit "708192a3b4c5d6e7f809122334455667"
      PaymentSplit "8192a3b4c5d6e7f80912233445566778"
